# neorv32_trng

**Purpose (model):** Top-level TRNG IP: accepts bus requests to control and read the generator, instantiates a neoTRNG entropy source and a FIFO buffer, forwards generated bytes into the FIFO, and returns status or FIFO bytes on bus reads.

## Use-case flows

| flow | value | path | lines (cited / in RTL) |
|---|---|---|---|
| configure | control bits written from the bus into local registers (enable, fifo_clr) |  | 4 / 4 |
| start | the stored enable bit is delivered to the neoTRNG instance and enables sampling (cell enable chain) |  | 3 / 3 |
| operate | neoTRNG debiasing and sampling assemble debiased bits into an 8-bit sample (sample_sreg), present it on data_o and, when valid, drive FIFO write (wdata/we) |  | 14 / 14 |
| read out | status read: returns enable, FIFO size, simulation flag and fifo.avail |  | 5 / 5 |
| read out | data read: return a random byte from FIFO.rdata when FIFO reports available, otherwise zeros |  | 4 / 4 |
| report | bus response signalling (ack, err, default data) produced each cycle for requests |  | 3 / 3 |
| reset | registers and internal state forced to known values when rstn_i = '0' (top-level and submodules) |  | 7 / 7 |

## Concept: Sampling enable setting that gates TRNG sampling

- confidentiality: yes-assumed, line 109 `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_en_c)                                  <= enable;` via bus_rsp_o.data -- The enable bit is returned on a bus read at bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_en_c) (line 109), so an external master can learn the stored setting and the integrator may treat it as secret.
- integrity: yes-rtl, line 105 `enable   <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` via bus_req_i.data -- enable is written by a bus write at line 105 (bus_req_i.data under bus_req_i.stb/rw) and that write can occur while sampling is active (enable fed into neoTRNG at line 137 and sampled into sample_en at line 354), so external writes can change it during operation.
- availability: yes-rtl, line 170 `fifo.clear <= '1' when (enable = '0') or (fifo_clr = '1') else '0';` via bus_req_i.data -- enable is used in the combinational clear expression fifo.clear <= '1' when (enable = '0') or (fifo_clr = '1') else '0' (line 170), so an external master that can set enable (via bus_req_i) can force FIFO clear and prevent progress.
- undermined behavior: no, line 105 `enable   <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` via bus_req_i.data -- enable has a single runtime driver from the bus write at line 105 (plus reset at line 95) and there is no debug/test override or alternate driver in the RTL.

| element | entity | role | occurrence -> line | edge | status | why | reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| enable | neorv32_trng | stores | 3 -> 105 `enable   <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` | CLOCKED_BY clk_i | verified |  | hit |
| sample_en | neoTRNG | stores | 4 -> 354 `sample_en <= enable_i;` | CLOCKED_BY clk_i | verified |  | not listed |

Influence points (code, from the map's GATED_BY / SELECTED_BY / CONSTRAINED_BY records): enable <- bus_req_i.rw, bus_req_i.stb

## Concept: FIFO-clear control decision that empties the FIFO (clear asserted when enable='0' or fifo_clr='1')

- confidentiality: yes-assumed, line 112 `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_avail_c)                               <= fifo.avail;` via bus_rsp_o.data -- The FIFO-clear decision affects FIFO availability which is reported at bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_avail_c) (line 112) and thus an external master can learn when the FIFO has been cleared.
- integrity: yes-rtl, line 106 `fifo_clr <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_fifo_clr_c);` via bus_req_i.data -- fifo_clr is written by a bus write at line 106 (bus_req_i.data) and fifo.clear is combinationally derived at line 170, so an external write can assert clear and remove buffered entropy (connected to FIFO at line 157).
- availability: yes-rtl, line 170 `fifo.clear <= '1' when (enable = '0') or (fifo_clr = '1') else '0';` via bus_req_i.data -- The condition that drives FIFO clear is explicit at line 170 (fifo.clear asserted when enable='0' or fifo_clr='1') and both sources are controllable from the bus, so an external master can force or block FIFO availability.
- undermined behavior: no, line 170 `fifo.clear <= '1' when (enable = '0') or (fifo_clr = '1') else '0';` via fifo.clear -- fifo.clear is driven by a single combinational expression at line 170 and the RTL contains no alternate debug/test override or secondary driver for this signal.

| element | entity | role | occurrence -> line | edge | status | why | reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fifo_clr | neorv32_trng | stores | 4 -> 106 `fifo_clr <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_fifo_clr_c);` | CLOCKED_BY clk_i | verified |  | hit |
| fifo.clear | neorv32_trng | computes | 3 -> 170 `fifo.clear <= '1' when (enable = '0') or (fifo_clr = '1') else '0';` | GATED_BY fifo_clr | verified |  | not listed |

Influence points (code, from the map's GATED_BY / SELECTED_BY / CONSTRAINED_BY records): fifo_clr <- bus_req_i.rw, bus_req_i.stb; fifo.clear <- enable, fifo_clr

## Concept: Random sample bytes (entropy) produced by neoTRNG and delivered through the FIFO to bus reads

- confidentiality: yes-assumed, line 117 `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_data_msb_c downto ctrl_data_lsb_c) <= fifo.rdata;` via bus_rsp_o.data -- The sampled bytes are propagated to the FIFO and returned to an external master on bus reads at bus_rsp_o.data when fifo.avail='1' (line 117), so external parties can learn these bytes and they may be considered confidential.
- integrity: yes-rtl, line 106 `fifo_clr <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_fifo_clr_c);` via bus_req_i.data -- An external bus write sets fifo_clr at line 106 (bus_req_i.data) and fifo.clear (line 170) is connected to the FIFO clear input (line 157), allowing an external master to remove or alter buffered bytes produced by the TRNG at runtime.
- availability: yes-rtl, line 170 `fifo.clear <= '1' when (enable = '0') or (fifo_clr = '1') else '0';` via bus_req_i.data -- fifo.clear is asserted at line 170 when enable='0' or fifo_clr='1' (both controllable from the bus), which clears the FIFO (connected at line 157) and so an external actor can prevent bytes from being available to consumers.
- undermined behavior: no, line 360 `sample_sreg <= sample_sreg(6 downto 0) & (sample_sreg(7) xor debias_data);` via sample_sreg -- Sample bytes are produced by the sample_sreg update and passed to the FIFO (sample_sreg update at line 360 and data_o at line 366) and the RTL contains no alternate debug/test bypass that substitutes or redirects the produced bytes at runtime.

| element | entity | role | occurrence -> line | edge | status | why | reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sample_sreg | neoTRNG | stores | 4 -> 360 `sample_sreg <= sample_sreg(6 downto 0) & (sample_sreg(7) xor debias_data);` | CLOCKED_BY clk_i | verified |  | not listed |
| data_o | neoTRNG | exit port | 2 -> 366 `data_o  <= sample_sreg;` | COPIES sample_sreg | verified |  | hit |
| fifo.rdata | neorv32_trng | computes | 3 -> 166 `rdata_o => fifo.rdata,` | CONNECTS rnd_pool_fifo_inst.rdata_o | edge, role unfit | CONNECTS does not demonstrate 'computes' | not listed |

Influence points (code, from the map's GATED_BY / SELECTED_BY / CONSTRAINED_BY records): sample_sreg <- debias_valid, sample_cnt, sample_en

## Concept: FIFO availability flag indicating whether buffered random bytes exist

- confidentiality: yes-assumed, line 112 `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_avail_c)                               <= fifo.avail;` via bus_rsp_o.data -- fifo.avail is reported to an external master at bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_avail_c) (line 112) and thus external observers can learn whether buffered bytes exist.
- availability: yes-rtl, line 170 `fifo.clear <= '1' when (enable = '0') or (fifo_clr = '1') else '0';` via fifo.clear -- fifo.clear is asserted by (enable='0') or (fifo_clr='1') at line 170 and is connected to the FIFO clear input at line 157, so external writes to fifo_clr or clearing via enable can force availability low and prevent progress.
- undermined behavior: no, line 167 `avail_o => fifo.avail` via rnd_pool_fifo_inst.avail_o -- fifo.avail is sourced solely from the FIFO instance output avail_o (line 167) and the RTL contains no runtime debug/test override that replaces this signal.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fifo.avail | neorv32_trng | computes | 4 -> 167 `avail_o => fifo.avail` | CONNECTS rnd_pool_fifo_inst.avail_o | edge, role unfit | CONNECTS does not demonstrate 'computes' | hit |

## Concept: Data-ready indicator (valid) produced by neoTRNG that triggers FIFO writes

- confidentiality: yes-assumed, line 117 `bus_rsp_o.data(ctrl_data_msb_c downto ctrl_data_lsb_c) <= fifo.rdata;` via bus_rsp_o.data -- valid_o causes FIFO writes (mapped at line 162) and those writes result in data visible to an external master on bus reads (bus_rsp_o.data at line 117), so the timing/occurrence of valid events can be inferred externally.
- integrity: yes-rtl, line 105 `enable   <= bus_req_i.data(ctrl_en_c);` via bus_req_i.data -- An external bus write can change enable (line 105), sample_en is assigned from enable at line 354 and the sampling logic resets sample_cnt when sample_en='0' (lines 355-357), so external writes can change valid_o (line 367) while the TRNG operates.
- availability: yes-rtl, line 355 `if (sample_en = '0') or (sample_cnt(sample_cnt'left) = '1') then` via sample_en / bus_req_i.data -- The sampling_control clears sample_cnt and sample_sreg when sample_en='0' (the condition at line 355), and sample_en is driven from enable (line 354) which is controllable via bus writes, so an external actor can stop valid events and block FIFO writes.
- undermined behavior: no, line 367 `valid_o <= sample_cnt(sample_cnt'left);` via valid_o -- valid_o is driven directly from the sample counter at line 367 and there is no alternate debug/test assignment to substitute or bypass this indicator in the RTL.

| element | entity | role | occurrence -> line | edge | status | why | reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| valid_o | neoTRNG | computes | 2 -> 367 `valid_o <= sample_cnt(sample_cnt'left);` | DERIVES_FROM sample_cnt | verified |  | hit |
